q: Super-rigidity for products: if Γ = Γ₁ × Γ₂ is a product of lattices, Margulis's theorem on 'commensurating superrigidity' shows that homomorphisms from Γ to GL(n,ℝ) that are:
opts: Non-trivial on both factors must extend to G₁ × G₂
Non-trivial on exactly one factor must factor through the projection to that factor (Margulis's factor theorem)
Determined by their restriction to the center
exp: Margulis's factor theorem for irreducible lattices Γ ≤ G₁×G₂: any irreducible lattice is algebraically 'indivisible' — homomorphisms from Γ to other groups cannot factor through either projection alone. This is a form of 'algebraic irreducibility' and is the basis for arithmeticity proofs.
